method_card.title: Music and Listening Habits
steps: Learn the key vocabulary for music genres, instruments and concerts
Master comparatives (plus / moins ... que) to compare music styles
Use depuis + present tense to say how long you have been doing something
Build extended sentences combining opinions, comparatives and time expressions
method_card.content:
This lesson covers music vocabulary, listening habits and how to talk about concerts, using comparatives and the depuis + present tense construction.

FrenchEnglish
la musiquemusic
écouter de la musiqueto listen to music
un chanteur / une chanteusea singer (male/female)
un groupea band
une chansona song
un concerta concert
un instrumentan instrument
jouer de la guitareto play the guitar
jouer du pianoto play the piano
le pop / le rock / le rappop / rock / rap
le jazz / le classiquejazz / classical
télécharger une chansonto download a song
talentueux / talentueusetalented
bruyant(e)noisy / loud
émouvant(e) (Higher)moving / touching

Comparatives: plus + adjective + que = more ... than; moins + adjective + que = less ... than; aussi + adjective + que = as ... as. Adjective still agrees with the noun it describes: Le rock est plus bruyant que le jazz. (Rock is louder than jazz.) La pop est aussi populaire que le rap. (Pop is as popular as rap.)

Depuis + present tense: Use depuis + the present tense to say how long something has been going on (and still is): Je joue de la guitare depuis trois ans. (I have been playing the guitar for three years.) Note: in English this uses a past tense, but in French the present tense is used.

Model paragraph: J'écoute de la musique depuis des années. Je préfère le pop parce qu'il est plus accessible que le jazz. Mon groupe préféré est très talentueux et leurs chansons sont émouvantes. (I have been listening to music for years. I prefer pop because it is more accessible than jazz. My favourite band is very talented and their songs are moving.)

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — music and entertainment appear across all papers

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'J'écoute du rap tous les jours. Je pense que c'est plus intéressant que le classique.'

steps.label: Break it down
steps.content: J'écoute du rap | tous les jours | Je pense que | c'est plus intéressant que le classique.

steps.label: Key vocabulary
steps.content: J'écoute = I listen to. du rap = rap (partitive: du + rap). tous les jours = every day. Je pense que = I think that.

steps.label: The comparative
steps.content: plus intéressant que = more interesting than. The structure is: plus + adjective + que.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: I listen to rap every day. I think it is more interesting than classical music.

worked_examples.question: How does depuis + present tense work? Translate: 'She has been playing the piano for two years.'

steps.label: Spot the structure
steps.content: English uses a past tense ('has been playing') but French uses the present tense with depuis: the action started in the past and is still going on.

steps.label: Build the sentence
steps.content: Subject + present tense verb + depuis + time period: Elle joue du piano depuis deux ans.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Elle joue du piano depuis deux ans. — present tense of jouer + depuis + duration.

bronze.question: Match the French music words to the English meaning
Match the French music genres and expressions to the English meaning
Complete the sentence with the correct comparative
sentence_parts: À mon avis, le rock est
le jazz. Je préfère le jazz car il est plus calme.

gaps.correct_explain: plus starts the 'more than' comparative: plus + adjective + que.

wrong.moins: moins means 'less'. The sentence says rock is louder (plus bruyant) than jazz, not less noisy.
wrong.aussi: aussi means 'as ... as'. The sentence is comparing unequals, so use plus.

wrong.de: de is a preposition (of/from), not used in comparatives. Use que for 'than'.
wrong.qu': qu' is used before a vowel or silent h — use que before the consonant le.

bronze.question: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the verb and depuis
sentence_parts: quatre ans. Il est très talentueux.

gaps.correct_explain: joue is the il/elle form of jouer in the present tense. With depuis, French uses the present, not the past, even when English uses 'has been playing'.

wrong.a joué: a joué is the perfect tense (he played). With depuis for an action still continuing, use the present: joue.
wrong.jouait: jouait is the imperfect (he used to play). Depuis + present shows the action is still ongoing: joue.

gaps.correct_explain: depuis means 'for' or 'since' when an action started in the past and continues now.

wrong.pendant: pendant means 'for' with a completed action in the past. Depuis is used with the present for actions still going on.

bronze.question: What does 'J'écoute de la musique depuis cinq ans' mean?
options: I have been listening to music for five years
I listened to music five years ago
I will listen to music for five years
I used to listen to music five years ago

bronze.question: Which sentence correctly says 'This song is less interesting than that one'?
options: Cette chanson est moins intéressante que celle-là.
Cette chanson est plus intéressante que celle-là.
Cette chanson est moins intéressant que celle-là.
Cette chanson est aussi intéressante que celle-là.

bronze.source_text: Mon chanteur préféré est très talentueux. J'écoute ses chansons tous les jours.
model_answers: My favourite singer is very talented. I listen to his songs every day.

bronze.question: Listen and type what you hear
bronze.audio_text: J'aime écouter du rock depuis longtemps.
bronze.correct_text: J'aime écouter du rock depuis longtemps.

silver.question: Complete the sentence by typing the correct word
silver.english: We arrived late at the concert last night.
sentence_parts: en retard au concert hier soir.

gaps.correct_explain: sommes arrivés is the perfect tense of arriver with être. Past participle agrees with nous: add -s for plural. Use arrivées for an all-female group.

wrong.avons arrivé: arriver uses être as auxiliary, not avoir. Use sommes arrivés.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Ma chanteuse préféré est très populaire.
silver.explanation: chanteuse is feminine, so the adjective must agree: préféré → préférée (add -e for feminine).
silver.translation: My favourite singer is very popular.

silver.question: Build the sentence in French
silver.english: I went to a concert last year.

distractor_labels.ai: wrong auxiliary — aller uses être in the perfect tense, not avoir. Je suis allé, not j'ai allé

silver.source_text: I have been playing the piano for two years. I think it is more difficult than the guitar.
model_answers: Je joue du piano depuis deux ans. Je pense que c'est plus difficile que la guitare.
Je joue du piano depuis deux ans. Je trouve que c'est plus difficile que la guitare.
hints: to play the piano = jouer du piano (depuis + present for 'have been playing')
I think = je pense que / je trouve que
more difficult than = plus difficile que

silver.audio_text: Je suis allé à un concert de pop le mois dernier.
silver.correct_text: Je suis allé à un concert de pop le mois dernier.
silver.translation: I went to a pop concert last month.

silver.question: Put these words in the correct order to form a sentence

gold.source_text: Last Saturday I went to a pop concert with my sister. The atmosphere was fantastic and the singer was very talented. I prefer pop music because it is more accessible than classical music.
model_answers: Samedi dernier, je suis allé(e) à un concert de pop avec ma sœur. L'ambiance était fantastique et la chanteuse était très talentueuse. Je préfère la musique pop parce qu'elle est plus accessible que la musique classique.

Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences about grammar accuracy","improvement":"optional specific correction"}

gold.question: Build the sentence in French
gold.english: She has been playing the guitar for three years and she is very talented.

distractor_labels.a joué: wrong tense — depuis + present tense is used for an action still continuing. Use joue (present), not a joué (perfect)
distractor_labels.talentueux: wrong gender — elle is feminine, so the adjective must be talentueuse not talentueux
distractor_labels.du: wrong article — guitare is feminine, so jouer de la guitare not jouer du guitare

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are at a leisure centre where a music event is being organised. You speak to the receptionist about the event.

bullets.prompt: Greet the receptionist and ask what musical events are on this week.
bullets.model_answer: Bonjour ! Quels événements musicaux y a-t-il cette semaine, s'il vous plaît ?
bullets.note: quels événements (what events) + y a-t-il (question inversion) + cette semaine

bullets.prompt: Say what music you prefer and how long you have been listening to it.
bullets.model_answer: Je préfère le rock et j'écoute ce genre de musique depuis trois ans.
bullets.note: je préfère + depuis + present tense (j'écoute — not perfect tense)

bullets.prompt: Ask if there are tickets available and how much they cost.
bullets.model_answer: Est-ce qu'il reste des billets ? Combien ça coûte ?
bullets.note: est-ce qu'il reste (are there still) + combien ça coûte (how much does it cost)

bullets.prompt: Say you will come back tomorrow and that you would like to bring a friend.
bullets.model_answer: Je reviendrai demain et je voudrais amener un ami.
bullets.note: je reviendrai (simple future — revenir) + je voudrais + infinitive

gold.question: Listen and type what you hear
gold.audio_text: Mon groupe préféré est très talentueux. Je les écoute depuis deux ans et leurs concerts sont toujours incroyables.
gold.correct_text: Mon groupe préféré est très talentueux. Je les écoute depuis deux ans et leurs concerts sont toujours incroyables.
gold.translation: My favourite band is very talented. I have been listening to them for two years and their concerts are always incredible.

gold.question: Complete the sentence by typing the correct word
gold.english: The singer whom I like most has released a new album.
sentence_parts: je préfère a sorti un nouvel album.

gaps.correct_explain: que (or qu' before a vowel) is used when the relative pronoun is the object of the clause. Here, je préfère la chanteuse — she is the object of préférer, so use que.

wrong.qui: qui is used for the subject of the relative clause (the thing doing the action). Here the singer is the object of je préfère, so use que.
